discovery.none: Nothing to discover: the car is reached through its OBD-II connector. What a phone scans for is the ADAPTER plugged into that connector -- see obd2-bluetooth-adapter.yaml for how adapters are found. The LeLink-class FFE0/FFE1 serial service that py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble uses is a post-connect route there (GATT family C), not a scan-time identity: the HM-10 layout is shared with unrelated devices. The generation is identified by querying the car (the group 0x01 reply length), not by finding it.

device.name: Nissan Leaf (ZE0 / AZE0 / ZE1) battery diagnostics
device.notes:
Nissan is an active manufacturer and still sells the Leaf. What ended is a cloud service: Nissan stopped the NissanConnect EV app on 30 March 2026 for Leafs built up to May 2019 (and e-NV200 vans), per its UK, Irish and Cypriot ownership pages. The app is what gave owners remote charge status and remote charging. The car's own diagnostic bus was never part of that service, and it still answers.
This spec covers that local path. A phone or a home server talks to a plug-in ELM327-class OBD-II adapter, usually a BLE one (see obd2-bluetooth-adapter.yaml for the adapter side). Through it the client polls the Li-ion Battery Controller (LBC, the pack's BMS) on CAN ID 0x79B and reads the answer on 0x7BB. The polls are KWP2000-style ReadDataByLocalIdentifier requests (service 0x21) that the community calls "groups". The answers are ISO-TP multi-frame. Group 0x01 carries state of charge, a health figure, the pack's Ah capacity, HV pack voltage and current. Group 0x02 has the 96 cell voltages, group 0x04 the pack temperatures, and group 0x61 the health block that ZE1 cars use for SOH. A few vehicle-level values (12 V battery, charge counters, gear, plug state) come from the VCM on 0x797 / 0x79A with UDS ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22). The odometer and tyre pressures come from the meter on 0x743 / 0x763.
GENERATIONS. The group 0x01 layout differs by generation, and the length the LBC announces in its first frame tells them apart: 0x29 (41 bytes) on ZE0, 0x2B (43) on AZE0 and 0x35 (53) on ZE1. Decode tables are therefore given per generation under protocol_details.lbc_groups. The generation names follow the community spreadsheet's README: ZE0 for 2010-2012 24 kWh cars, AZE0 for 2013-2017 24/30 kWh cars, ZE1 for 2018+ 40/62 kWh cars. OVMS documentation calls AZE0 "ZE0" too, so check the model year, not the label.
READ-ONLY SCOPE. This document carries reads only. The same open sources also implement LBC writes: clearing DTCs, and a session, security-access and routine sequence that resets the pack's degradation history. Those are left out on purpose and listed by service only under protocol_details.excluded_services. They change what the car reports about its own battery, and the people relying on this spec are often deciding whether to buy a used Leaf.
ZE1 PORT ISOLATION. On ZE1 cars a CAN gateway sits between the OBD-II port and the vehicle buses, and it powers down when the ignition is off. With the car off the port goes quiet and polls go unanswered. OVMS documents this, and so does the py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble README ("the car must be on"). ZE0/AZE0 ports stay reachable with the car off.
CONFIDENCE: every byte offset below is transcribed from open-source code or the community spreadsheet (verification: reported), or inferred from their sample dumps (hypothesis). This project has not polled a car.

exclusivity.recovery: One tester at a time on the connector. Unplug any other OBD-II dongle or telematics device (an OVMS module, an insurance dongle) before polling, because their requests to the same ECUs interleave with this client's and corrupt the multi-frame replies.

pairing.notes: Nothing gates the documented surface. The LBC answers the 0x21 group reads on a bare connection, with no diagnostic session and no SecurityAccess, and the car stores nothing about the client: OVMS and Battery-Emulator send these polls cold. The only physical precondition is power state. A ZE1's CAN gateway isolates the port until the car is switched on (see setup). The operations that ARE gated (Battery- Emulator's degradation-history reset, which runs a SecurityAccess seed/key exchange) are writes, and this spec leaves them out (see protocol_details.excluded_services). Any Bluetooth pairing belongs to the adapter, not the car: see obd2-bluetooth-adapter.yaml.

safety_advisory.detail: These requests are read-only, but they still go onto a working car's buses. Follow the open clients this spec is taken from. The py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble Home Assistant integration polls every 10 s while the car is on. When it finds the car off it backs off to 5 minutes, because on some cars each poll of a sleeping car clicks a relay and frequent polling wears it out. OVMS does not poll the LBC at all while the car is off. On ZE1 it polls the balancing-shunt group only while charging, to keep traffic down while driving. Battery-Emulator stops its own polling while another tool (Leaf Spy, for example) is querying 0x79B. It also never starts a group transfer while one is in flight, because the LBC drops a request that arrives while it is still sending a reply. Do not send the excluded write services. This is an independent, experimental client unaffiliated with Nissan; the vehicle's own instructions govern. Leave the adapter unplugged when not in use unless its own documentation says it is safe to leave in place.
safety_advisory.summary: Diagnostic polling adds traffic on the car's buses and can wake modules; poll gently, never alongside another tester, and only the read requests listed here.

credentials.notes: Access control is physical: whoever reaches the connector can read these groups. None of the reads here needs a diagnostic session or SecurityAccess (OVMS and Battery-Emulator send the 0x21 polls cold).

factory_reset.effect: Not applicable. A car reached over a diagnostic connector holds no credentials or pairing state for a client to clear. The LBC's degradation-history reset that some open tools implement is a write to the battery controller, not a return to an unprovisioned state, and it is out of scope for this read-only spec (see protocol_details.excluded_services).

methods.description: Plug an ELM327-class adapter into the OBD-II connector, wake the car (ZE1: switch it on), connect to the adapter and run the ELM327 initialisation. There is no pairing or credential exchange with the car.

steps.action: Plug the adapter into the car's OBD-II connector.
steps.expect: The adapter powers up from the connector.

steps.action: On a ZE1 (2018+) car, switch the car on. ZE0/AZE0 cars answer with the car off, but polling a sleeping car may wake modules; see the safety advisory.
steps.notes: The ZE1 CAN gateway isolates the port with the ignition off (OVMS documentation; py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble README).

steps.action: Connect to the adapter (BLE GATT serial pipe or Classic SPP) and send the initialisation in protocol_details.elm327_session.
Poll LBC group 0x01 and identify the generation from the first-frame length (0x29 ZE0, 0x2B AZE0, 0x35 ZE1).

setup.notes: Nothing to provision on the car. The setup that matters is the adapter's (pairing, if any) and the ELM327 session initialisation, which is recorded in protocol_details.elm327_session.

rejoin.notes: Switching adapter or host is a physical swap. The car keeps no record of which tool last connected.

evidence.open_questions: The AZE0 SOC offset, the ZE1 group 0x01 health word, the group 0x06 bit layout and whether ZE0/AZE0 answer group 0x61 are unresolved; see remaining_unknowns.
evidence.public_research: Facts were transcribed from four open sources, read but not executed. (1) dalathegreat/leaf_can_bus_messages: the README's ECU request/response table and worked VCM example, and the canmsgs.xlsx sheets "79b-7bb" (group layouts) and "797-79a". (2) OVMS vehicle_nissanleaf: poll lists per generation, reply lengths, and decoders for groups 01/02/04/06/61 and VCM DIDs. (3) dalathegreat/Battery-Emulator NISSAN-LEAF-BATTERY: frame-by-frame decoders keyed on the group 0x01 length, group 0x61/0x62/0x83/0x84, DTC read, and native-CAN flow control. (4) py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble, the library behind the nissan-leaf-obd-ble Home Assistant integration: the ELM327 init and header sequence over BLE, the VCM/meter DID table and the ZE1 group 0x01 decoder. Leaf Spy, the closed commercial app, was not examined.

adapter_requirements: Custom request headers (ATSH 79B / 797 / 743): none of these ECUs answers the functional 0x7DF broadcast.
Multi-frame ISO-TP receive: group 0x01 is 6-8 frames, group 0x02 is 29 frames and group 0x61 is 48 frames (331 bytes, a 12-bit first-frame length).
Client-addressed flow control: the flow-control frame must go to the LBC's request ID 0x79B (ATFCSH 79B), not the default 0x7E0.

Timing: the community spreadsheet says the flow-control frame must follow the LBC's first frame within 15 ms. Battery-Emulator, on a native CAN interface, answers each frame with 30 01 00, a block size of 1.

Clone ELM327 firmware is untested here; py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble's defaults are for the LeLink BLE dongle (its README), and its Home Assistant community thread is about the LeLink 2. No other adapter is reported.

connector.model_years: All generations (2010+). On ZE1 the port sits behind a CAN gateway that powers down with the ignition off.

data_identifiers.name: VCM power switch state (bit 7 of the data byte set = on)
VCM gear position (1 Park, 2 Reverse, 3 Neutral, 4 Drive; Eco is 5 or 7, sources disagree)
VCM 12 V battery current (signed 16-bit, 1/256 A per bit)
VCM L0/L1/L2 (AC) charge count; 0xFFFF = no value
VCM ambient temperature
data_identifiers.source: py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble. The community spreadsheet's 797-79a sheet instead reads this DID as degrees F + 41, at a different byte; unresolved.

data_identifiers.name: VCM J1772 plug state (0 not plugged, 1 partially plugged, 2 plugged)
VCM charging mode (0 not charging, 1 L1, 2 L2, 3 L3/quick)
VCM motor RPM (signed 16-bit; the source marks its parser as needing a fix)
Meter tyre pressure front right (0.25 psi per bit)
data_identifiers.source: py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble; 0x0E26 front left, 0x0E27 rear right, 0x0E28 rear left decode the same way

ecus.name: VCM (vehicle control module)
owns: gear position, power switch, plug state, charge mode

requests.description: LBC group 0x01: HV current, HV pack voltage, 12 V supply, insulation resistance, Hx/SOH, SOC and Ah capacity. Reply length identifies the generation; decode with protocol_details.lbc_groups.group_01.
requests.name: lbc_group_01_battery_summary
requests.notes: Sent to 0x79B, answered on 0x7BB. Single frame on the wire: 02 21 01 (padding FF or 00).

requests.description: LBC group 0x02: 96 cell voltages, then pack and bus voltage. 198-byte reply (first frame 10 C6).
requests.name: lbc_group_02_cell_voltages

requests.description: LBC group 0x04: pack thermistor raw values and per-sensor temperatures. 16 bytes on ZE0/AZE0, 31 on ZE1.
requests.name: lbc_group_04_temperatures

requests.description: LBC group 0x06: cell balancing-shunt status. 26-byte reply. Bit layout is disputed between sources; see remaining_unknowns.
requests.name: lbc_group_06_balancing_shunts

requests.description: LBC group 0x61: Hx, SOH, dash capacity bars, unfiltered and filtered SOH and (ZE1) pack capacity. 331-byte reply, so the first frame is 11 4B. OVMS polls it on ZE1 only; whether ZE0/AZE0 answer is not established.
requests.name: lbc_group_61_health_block

requests.description: LBC group 0x62: lifetime L1/L2 and quick-charge counts, then usage histograms. 0x76 bytes on ZE0/AZE0, 0x78 on ZE1.
requests.name: lbc_group_62_charge_counters

requests.description: LBC group 0x83: battery part number, 7 ASCII characters at payload[2..8].
requests.name: lbc_group_83_part_number

requests.description: LBC group 0x84: battery pack serial number, 16 ASCII characters at payload[2..17].
requests.name: lbc_group_84_pack_serial
requests.notes: A per-pack identifier. Treat it like a VIN: do not publish one read from a real car.

requests.description: Read the LBC's stored DTCs: UDS ReadDTCInformation, reportDTCByStatusMask, mask 0x0E. Reply 59 02 <availability mask>, then 4 bytes per DTC (3-byte code and 1 status byte).
requests.name: lbc_read_dtc
requests.notes: From Battery-Emulator. Do not run it at the same time as a group transfer: the LBC drops a request that lands while it is still answering another.

requests.description: VCM UDS ReadDataByIdentifier. Send 22 <DID hi> <DID lo> to 0x797; the reply on 0x79A is 62 <DID hi> <DID lo> <data>. DIDs and decodes are in obd.data_identifiers.
requests.name: vcm_read_did

requests.description: Meter (M&A) UDS ReadDataByIdentifier, sent to 0x743 and answered on 0x763; see the 0x0Exx entries in obd.data_identifiers.
requests.name: meter_read_did

requests.description: VIN from the VCM: 21 81 sent to 0x797. 19-byte reply after 61 81: 17 ASCII VIN characters and 2 zero bytes.
requests.name: vcm_read_vin
requests.notes: AZE0 cars may return 0x1B (ESC) characters; OVMS replaces them with spaces. Never publish a real VIN.

conventions.decode: value = raw * scale / divisor + value_offset, where raw is the big-endian integer at [byte_offset, byte_offset + length), read as two's complement when signed is true. Missing scale/divisor default to 1 and value_offset to 0.
conventions.payload_offsets: Every offset in lbc_groups counts bytes of the REASSEMBLED ISO-TP payload, with payload[0] the positive-response service byte (0x61) and payload[1] the group number. This is the convention of py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble and of Battery-Emulator's "payload[n]" comments. OVMS indexes from the byte after the group number, so an OVMS offset is this offset minus 2. The community spreadsheet counts per CAN frame. Its "line n, Dk" is payload[6 + 7*(n-1) + (k-1)] for n >= 1; in the first frame (line 0), Dk is payload[k-2].
conventions.sentinels: 0xFF-filled bytes are padding. 0xFFFF in a cell-voltage or thermistor slot means "no reading" (Battery-Emulator), and 0xFFFF in a charge counter means no value (OVMS).

ble_default_gatt.notes: The LeLink/LeLink2 defaults the library ships. Other adapters need their own UUIDs (the integration makes all three configurable); see obd2-bluetooth-adapter.yaml for the adapter GATT families.

init.expect: anything (the reply can be junk); wait 1 s

init.purpose: show CAN IDs, so 0x7BB / 0x79A / 0x763 replies can be told apart
CAN auto-formatting off: the client writes the ISO-TP PCI byte itself and reassembles replies itself
optional: the library treats < 6 V as the adapter not being in a live socket

elm327_session.native_can_flow_control: Clients on a raw CAN interface (Battery-Emulator) answer each frame from 0x7BB with "30 01 00 FF FF FF FF FF" on 0x79B. That is block size 1, so one consecutive frame per flow control. The spreadsheet says it must be sent within 15 ms of the frame it answers.

per_ecu_header.description: Sent whenever the target ECU changes (the library caches the last header). <hdr> is the request ID without 0x: 79B, 797 or 743.
per_ecu_header.notes: ATFCSD 30 00 00 is a ContinueToSend flow-control frame with block size 0 (send everything) and STmin 0. ATFCSM 1 makes the adapter send that user-defined frame. The library sets no receive filter (no ATCRA); see remaining_unknowns.

elm327_session.request_format: Because CAN auto-formatting is off, every request carries its own single-frame PCI byte: "022101" is LBC group 0x01 (PCI 02, then 21 01); "03221156" is VCM DID 0x1156. Requests to the LBC are padded to 8 bytes on native-CAN clients (Battery-Emulator pads with 00, the spreadsheet with FF).

excluded_services.description: Services that the same open sources send and that this read-only spec deliberately does not carry as requests. They are named by service only, so a reader knows they exist and why they are absent.

entries.why: py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble sends 02 10 C0 first and calls it a mystery command. It treats no reply as "car off" and skips the remaining polls. It is a DiagnosticSessionControl into a Nissan-specific session. Battery-Emulator uses the same session request on the LBC as the first step of its degradation-history reset. Its effect on the VCM is undocumented. A read-only client can probe with VCM DID 0x1304 instead; whether that works as a wake probe on every generation is a hypothesis.
Clears stored battery DTCs (Battery-Emulator). A write.

Battery-Emulator's degradation-history (SOH) reset: session control, tester present, a SecurityAccess seed/key exchange and RoutineControl. It rewrites what the pack reports about its own health. Out of scope.

generation_by_group_01_length.0x2C: ZE1 shortly after wake-up; layout not mapped by any source -- poll again

protocol_details.iso_tp_reassembly: Frame type is the PCI high nibble. 0x0 is a single frame: the low nibble is the length and the data follows. 0x1 is a first frame: the 12-bit length is (PCI & 0x0F) << 8 | byte1 and 6 data bytes follow. Group 0x61's 331 bytes arrive as 11 4B. 0x2 is a consecutive frame: the low nibble is a sequence number running 1..F and wrapping to 0, and 7 data bytes follow. Concatenate in order and truncate to the announced length; the tail of the last frame is padding. A single frame 03 7F <service> <NRC> is a negative response. Battery-Emulator explicitly discards these, so they are never decoded as group data. Group 0x02 is longer than 16 frames, so the sequence number wraps more than once. Count frames, not sequence values, to know when the reply is complete.

fields.name: state_of_charge
fields.source: Assumed to share the ZE0 offset, as Hx and capacity do; no open client decodes SOC from the 0x2B layout

fields.name: hv_current_1
fields.source: Position from Battery-Emulator (all layouts, not decoded); scale from py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble's ZE1 decoder

fields.name: hv_pack_voltage
fields.source: py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble decodes this on ZE1; the 24 kWh sample dumps in OVMS give 395.61 V and 368.13 V at the same offset

fields.name: aux_12v_voltage
fields.source: Battery-Emulator (mV, same offset on every layout); the community spreadsheet notes this word as 'Acc V / 1024'

fields.name: capacity_ah
fields.source: Battery-Emulator (u32 at 34..37); OVMS reads the low 24 bits at 35..37

fields.name: hv_current_1
fields.source: py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble lbc decoder. Battery-Emulator notes 62 kWh owners found it unusable

fields.name: aux_12v_voltage
fields.source: Battery-Emulator (confirmed on its bench for ZE1)

fields.name: health_1024
fields.source: OVMS (Hx, citing Dala's 2018 Leaf CAN document) and py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble (hv_battery_health). Battery-Emulator disagrees: it reads no Hx from this layout and takes ZE1 Hx from group 0x61

cells.source: OVMS PollReply_BMS_Volt, Battery-Emulator, community spreadsheet group 2

group_04.notes: ZE1's 31-byte reply is decoded with the same first 16 bytes by OVMS, which calls its own ZE1 capture incomplete; the rest is unmapped.

sensors.raw_absent: 0xFFFF -- sensor 3 is absent on 2013+ packs, which have three sensors (Battery-Emulator)

raw_to_celsius.source: OVMS (linear approximation; Battery-Emulator uses its own raw-to-F conversion instead)

sensors.temp_byte: Whole degrees Celsius as reported by the LBC; signedness below 0 C not established

group_06.notes: Balancing-shunt flags for the 96 cells. The layout is disputed. OVMS reads 24 bytes (payload[2..25]) at 4 bits per byte: bit 3 = first cell of the byte, bit 0 = fourth ("shunt order 8421"). It then inverts the whole set. Battery-Emulator reads 12 bytes (payload[2..13]) at 8 bits per byte, with bit i of byte n = cell 8n + i. No decode is asserted here.

fields.name: soh_bar_count
fields.source: Battery-Emulator (reads 0xFF on a pack bench-tested off the car)

group_62.notes: payload[6..end] holds usage histograms whose per-generation offsets are not transcribed here.

polling_cadence.battery_emulator: One LBC group every 10 s in rotation (2 s for the first pass); static groups 0x62/0x83/0x84 dropped from the rotation once read.

ovms_ze1_seconds_by_state.car_on_or_driving: group 01/02 every 60 s, 04 every 180 s, 61 every 900 s

polling_cadence.py_nissan_leaf_obd_ble: Every 10 s with the car on; 5 min when the car looks off (the VCM probe got no reply); 1 h when the adapter is out of BLE range.

test_vectors.description: Invented values only -- no frame here was read from a real car. Each vector is the frame sequence an ELM327 with ATH1 prints (CAN ID, then 8 data bytes, spaces added for reading). scripts/test_nissan_leaf_obd2_spec.py reassembles it with the ISO-TP rules above and checks every decoded value against `expected`.

7BB 26 FF FF FF FF FF FF FF
7BB 27 FF FF FF FF FF FF FF

vcm_and_meter_single_frames.meaning: Park (the spreadsheet README's own worked example)

remaining_unknowns: AZE0 state-of-charge offset in group 0x01: assumed to equal ZE0's payload[31..33] because Hx and capacity share offsets, but no open client decodes SOC from the 0x2B layout.

ZE1 group 0x01 payload[30..31]: OVMS and py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble read it as Hx/'health' divided by 102.4; Battery-Emulator reads no Hx from this layout and uses group 0x61 instead. Which figure matches the dash or Leaf-Spy-style SOH is not established.

HV current and HV pack voltage on ZE0/AZE0: offsets taken from the ZE1 decoder and supported only by sample dumps (hypothesis). The current's sign test in py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble masks bit 27 (0x8000000) rather than bit 31, which gives the same result for realistic currents; full two's complement is assumed here.
The 12 V word at payload[22..23]: Battery-Emulator reads millivolts; the community spreadsheet's note says '/1024'. Millivolts is used here.
Group 0x06 balancing-shunt bit layout: OVMS (24 bytes, 4 bits each, order 8421, then inverted) and Battery-Emulator (12 bytes, 8 bits each, LSB first) disagree.
Whether ZE0/AZE0 answer group 0x61, and what its payload past byte 17 holds (331 bytes in total).
Group 0x04 on ZE1 (31 bytes): only the first 16 bytes are mapped, and OVMS calls its own capture incomplete. Whether the per-sensor temperature byte is signed below 0 C is not stated by any source.
The ZE1 group 0x01 reply of length 0x2C seen shortly after wake-up has no mapped layout.

How an ELM327 picks which CAN IDs to print when ATSH is 79B and no ATCRA filter is set: py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble sets none and works with the LeLink2. Adding ATCRA 7BB (or 79A / 763) is a plausible hardening, but a hypothesis.
Whether ELM327 firmware honours ATFCSH/ATFCSD/ATFCSM while CAN auto-formatting is off (ATCAF0), as the library configures, or whether the multi-frame reads succeed for another reason on the LeLink2.

Which OBD-II connector pins carry the bus that reaches the LBC on each generation. The spreadsheet says 0x79B answers on both EV-CAN and CAR-CAN and 0x797 on CAR-CAN only, but no source maps that to J1962 pins.
Gear-position code for Eco: 7 per the spreadsheet README, 5 per py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble.
VCM DID 0x115D ambient temperature: py-nissan-leaf-obd-ble uses data byte 3 as x/2 - 40 C; the spreadsheet's 797-79a sheet describes a degrees-F + 41 encoding at another byte.
Whether the VCM 10 C0 session probe the HA library sends has side effects, and whether a 22 13 04 read is an adequate read-only replacement as a wake probe.
e-NV200 vans share much of this stack per OVMS, but are not covered here.
